A also adds a test that pins down the duplicate-in-existing behavior. A reports a measured timing and a clean typecheck. B's report is honest but says it verified neither, and B adds no test for the edge case it describes.

No test covers the performance itself.

Speedup not measured on a realistic dataset.

verdict.rationale: Both changes make the same fix to mergeContacts: a Map from normalized email to index, built once and updated on append. Both keep first-match semantics for duplicates already in the book and still merge duplicates within the upload. B also adds a test for the duplicate-in-existing edge case, which A only mentions in its report. B's report also covers a measured timing and a clean typecheck, while A left both unverified.
a_issues: No test for the case where the existing book already holds duplicate emails, though the report calls it out as preserved behavior.
Typecheck not confirmed and no timing measured, so the speedup and type safety are asserted but not verified.
b_issues: The timing came from a throwaway script and no benchmark was committed, which the report acknowledges.
